author: TEDx Talks
description:
How do we listen to the stars without exhausting the Earth? In this TEDx talk, Robbe explains the incredible potential of the Einstein Telescope, why it matters, and how we can meet its energy demands responsibly in the context of the climate crisis. 

Dr. Ing. Robbe Breugelmans is a postdoctoral researcher at Hasselt University where he investigates how to power the Einstein Telescope with sustainable energy solutions. The Einstein Telescope is a proposed underground observatory designed to detect gravitational waves, faint ripples in spacetime that carry information from the most extreme events in the universe. Envisioned as Europe’s most advanced facility of its kind, it could potentially be hosted in Belgium. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What does the universe sound like? | Robbe Breugelmans | TEDxUHasselt
